question: What are the four core principles set out by MAS in 2018 for responsible AIDA use in Singapore’s financial sector
ideal_answer: The four FEAT principles are Fairness, Ethics, Accountability and Transparency. MAS published them in 2018 as 14 principles grouped under these four headings to guide firms using AI and data analytics (AIDA) to provide financial products and services.
notes: happy-path. Your Q1. Plain gpt-4o-mini invented a fifth principle ('Security') in W1.
source: FEAT Principles Final.pdf, p.6 (Summary of Principles)

question: Which statutory exceptions under the PDPA allow organizations to process personal data for AI development without fresh consent
ideal_answer: The guidelines name two exceptions an AI developer can rely on instead of consent: the Business Improvement Exception (enhancing an existing product, improving operational efficiency, or offering new or personalised products and services; it also covers sharing within a group of companies) and the Research Exception (commercial research to advance science and engineering without a product development roadmap; it also covers sharing between unrelated companies for joint research).
notes: happy-path. Your Q3.
source: Advisory Guidelines on the Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems.pdf, §4.2, pp.5-6

question: What four conditions must be met to rely on the PDPA's Research Exception
ideal_answer: To use personal data under the Research Exception: (a) the research purpose cannot reasonably be accomplished unless the data is in individually identifiable form; (b) there is a clear public benefit to using the data for the research; (c) the results will not be used to make any decision that affects the individual; and (d) if the results are published, they are published in a form that does not identify the individual. Disclosure for research additionally requires that it is impracticable to seek the individual's consent.
notes: happy-path. Your Q4. W4: gpt-4o-mini got about 1 of 4, gpt-4o 2 of 4.
source: Advisory Guidelines on Key Concepts in the PDPA_Apr2026.pdf, p.74

question: What are the four main dimensions of the Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
ideal_answer: The framework sets out four dimensions: (1) assess and bound the risks upfront; (2) make humans meaningfully accountable; (3) implement technical controls and processes; and (4) enable end-user responsibility.
notes: happy-path. Your Q6.
source: Mgf for Agentic AI (atx Release) July 2026.pdf, pp.3-4 (Executive Summary)

question: What is the primary role of SAFR in financial agentic AI deployments
ideal_answer: SAFR (Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime) is a reference approach for a runtime governance layer that operates at the point of action: it sits between the agent and the systems it acts on and evaluates proposed actions before they execute. It defines what each agentic system is authorised to do, how proposed actions are assessed at runtime, and what records are kept for review, accountability and remediation. MAS states it is not regulatory guidance or a supervisory expectation.
notes: happy-path. Your Q7. W3 UI demo: the model did not know SAFR.
source: SAFR v1.1.pdf, p.6 (Introduction)

question: What are the nine ecosystem dimensions established in the Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (2024)
ideal_answer: The nine dimensions are: Accountability; Data; Trusted Development and Deployment; Incident Reporting; Testing and Assurance; Security; Content Provenance; Safety and Alignment R&D; and AI for Public Good.
notes: happy-path. Your Q8. W4: neither model could list them.
source: Model-AI-Governance-Framework-for-Generative-AI-19-June-2024.pdf, p.2 (Contents)

question: What are the five stages of the AI lifecycle according to the MindForge Framework
ideal_answer: MindForge's AI lifecycle has five stages: (1) Use Case Context and Design; (2) Data Acquisition and Processing; (3) Onboarding, Build and Validation; (4) Deployment; and (5) Usage, Monitoring and Change Management. The stages are not strictly linear; moving between them is often iterative.
notes: happy-path. Your Q9.
source: MindForge AI Risk Management Operationalisation Handbook.pdf, PDF p.23 (printed p.16)

question: What specific function was the Veritas Initiative created to perform regarding the FEAT Principles
ideal_answer: Veritas (an MAS-led industry consortium) turns the FEAT principles into practical assessment methodologies so financial institutions can assess their AIDA systems against them. Phase 1 (January 2021) produced the initial Fairness assessment methodology with banking use cases (credit scoring, customer marketing); Phase 2 (from March 2021) extended it to banking and insurance and added methodologies for Ethics and Accountability (Document 3B) and Transparency (Document 3C).
notes: happy-path. Your Q10.
source: Veritas Document 3A - FEAT Fairness Principles Assessment Methodology.pdf, pp.4, 6-7

question: Under Part 9B of the PDPA, what specific actions constitute offences for egregious mishandling of personal data by individuals
ideal_answer: Part 9B makes it an offence for individuals to knowingly or recklessly: (a) disclose personal data without authorisation; (b) use personal data for a wrongful gain or a wrongful loss to any person; or (c) re-identify anonymised data.
notes: happy-path. Your Q11. W4: both models only partly right.
source: Advisory Guidelines on Key Concepts in the PDPA_Apr2026.pdf, p.9

question: What good practices are recommended under the PDPA for third-party Service Providers acting as data intermediaries during AI development
ideal_answer: Service Providers that process personal data on a customer's behalf act as data intermediaries. The guidelines call it good practice to (a) use data mapping and labelling at the pre-processing stage to track which data formed the training set, and (b) keep a provenance record of the training data's lineage: its source and how it was transformed during preparation. These help detect unauthorised access or changes to training data and help the customer meet its own notification, consent and accountability obligations.
notes: happy-path. Your Q12.
source: Advisory Guidelines on the Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems.pdf, §11.2-11.4, pp.19-20

question: What two measurable indicators are recommended in the Agentic AI Framework to audit human oversight effectiveness and signal rubber-stamping or review fatigue
ideal_answer: Two indicators: (1) the human override rate, meaning how often humans reject or modify agent actions (a low rate may signal rubber-stamping); and (2) human response time when reviewing agent actions (a shorter time may signal automation bias or review fatigue).
notes: happy-path. Your Q13. W4: gpt-4o right, gpt-4o-mini invented two.
source: Mgf for Agentic AI (atx Release) July 2026.pdf, p.30

question: What encryption algorithm and key length are recommended for long-term data retention in ICT systems
ideal_answer: The guide recommends AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) with a key length of at least 256 bits for long-term retention, reviewed periodically to make sure the method is still recognised as secure. Encryption keys should be kept secure and separate from the encrypted data.
notes: happy-path. Your Q15. W4: both models right.
source: guide-to-data-protection-practices-for-ict-systems.pdf, p.25

question: In the Veritas Transparency Methodology (Document 3C), what is the difference between proactive and reactive transparency
ideal_answer: Proactive transparency is the institution telling the general public, including current and prospective customers, that it uses their data and AIDA systems to engage them or make decisions about them (FEAT Principle 12). Reactive (or responsive) transparency is answering a data subject's request about a specific decision that affected them, such as why a loan was declined (FEAT Principles 13 and 14). Proactive transparency can be generic or instance-specific; reactive transparency is always instance-specific.
notes: happy-path. Your Q17.
source: Veritas Document 3C - FEAT Transparency Principles Assessment Methodology.pdf, p.11 (§2.2)

question: What five organizational roles are explicitly in scope for AI governance skills and capability enablers in the MindForge Operationalisation Handbook
ideal_answer: The five roles are Executives, Builders, Custodians, Use Case Owners and Business Users. Each has its own skill and knowledge needs for managing AI-specific risks.
notes: happy-path. Your Q20.
source: MindForge AI Risk Management Operationalisation Handbook.pdf, PDF p.115 (section 4, Enablers)

question: What fundamental restriction applies when a human user delegates runtime authority or permissions to an autonomous AI agent
ideal_answer: An agent's authority must stay within the authorising human's own permissions: a user should not give an agent more than the user is allowed to do (for example, access to data outside the user's permissions), and such delegations should be clearly recorded. Authorisations should also be scoped, least-privilege, time- or session-bound and non-transferable, with explicit escalation paths for more access (MGF for Agentic AI). SAFR expresses the delegation as a machine-readable mandate setting out what the agent may do, within what limits and under what conditions, and the agent cannot extend that mandate through its own reasoning.
notes: harder · multi-document. Your Q19. Needs the MGF for Agentic AI and SAFR together.
source: Mgf for Agentic AI (atx Release) July 2026.pdf, p.24; SAFR v1.1.pdf, p.12

question: How does the MindForge Framework distinguish between an AI "Model", an AI "System", and an AI "Use Case"
ideal_answer: A model is a mathematical or logical representation that maps inputs to outputs, such as an LLM predicting tokens or a credit-default model. A system is a model plus the software components that make it usable in the real world, such as a chatbot with a search engine; it may contain several models. A use case is the specific real-world context in which a system is intentionally used, such as underwriting loan risk. The handbook makes the use case the basic unit of AI governance and risk management, because with GenAI and agentic AI a model's risks depend on its use case and its system's guardrails.
notes: harder · three-way distinction plus why it matters. Your Q16.
source: MindForge AI Risk Management Operationalisation Handbook.pdf, PDF pp.22-23 (printed pp.15-16)

question: According to PDPA guidelines on AI Recommendation Systems, what three key elements should be included in consumer notifications at the point of data collection
ideal_answer: The guidelines list four items, not three, that organisations are encouraged to include in notifications where practicable: (a) the product function that needs personal data (e.g. movie recommendations); (b) a general description of the types of personal data collected (e.g. viewing history); (c) how processing that data is relevant to the product feature; and (d) the specific features of the data most likely to influence the feature (e.g. whether a movie was watched completely). Notifications should be proportionate to the risk and can be layered, for example a pop-up linking to a fuller policy.
notes: harder · false premise. Your Q18 asks for three elements, but the source lists four (a-d). A good answer corrects the premise.
source: Advisory Guidelines on the Use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems.pdf, §9.5-9.7, pp.13-14

question: What default human approval requirements are recommended for "Read", "Edit", and "Bash" agent actions
ideal_answer: In the Tencent CodeBuddy case study in the framework, approval defaults follow the risk of each action: Read (reading files, listing directories) needs no approval; Edit (modifying files) needs approval valid only for that session; and Bash (running shell commands) needs approval that is then permanent for the project or the command. The framework also lets users or organisations adjust these defaults to each project's risk, to avoid alert fatigue.
notes: harder · conditional, and the source is a case study, not the framework's own rule. Your Q14.
source: Mgf for Agentic AI (atx Release) July 2026.pdf, pp.30-31 (Tencent CodeBuddy case study)
